To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IKKα controls ATG16 stabilization to prevent endoplasmic stress during acute intestinal inflammation.
the IκB kinase complex is required for epithelial regeneration in the inflamed colon by controlling ATG16L-1 degradation to prevent endoplasmic stress.

the Ikk&agr;-dependent stabilization of ATG16 is critical for the regulation of the unfolded protein response (ER stress) and the subsequent induction of cytoprotectant cytokines, such as IL-18, in the context of intestinal inflammation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of IKKα in the control of ATG16l1 degradation to prevent endoplasmic stress during intestinal inflammation.
the role of the IKK complex in the regulation of the unfolded protein response in intestinal epithelial cells and the consequences thereof during acute inflammation.
the regulation of autophagy and its role in the pathogenesis of inflammatory bowel disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

IKK&agr;/NF-κB is a central regulator of the UPR in intestinal epithelial cells and that the UPR plays a central role in regulating intestinal homeostasis and epithelial regeneration during inflammation.

IKKα is a central mediator sensing cytokine and microbial stimuli to suppress endoplamsatic reticulum stress and thereby assuring anti-inflammatroy function during acute intestinal inflammatory responses.

IKKα is an important regulator of the unfolded protein response (and autophagy) in intestinal epithelial cells, which is important in the maintenance of intestinal homeostasis and the prevention of intestinal inflammation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IKK&agr;, a kinase involved in NF-&kgr;B activation, is a key regulator of intestinal regeneration after injury.

IKK&agr;, in addition to its well-established function in the regulation of inflammatory cytokines, also regulates the autophagy machinery and thus controls the unfolded protein response in epithelial cells.
the I&kgrave;kB kinase complex (Ikk`) is a critical regulator of intestinal epithelial homeostasis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IKK&agr;/NF-&kgr;B axis is a central regulator of epithelial cell homeostasis during intestinal inflammation.
the IκB kinase (IKK) complex has a previously unrecognized role in controlling endoplasmic-reticulum stress during intestinal inflammation.
we identified a novel mechanism of how inflammation is regulated in the intestine.
